item.text: I’m doing a quick design pass before editing. The remaining useful change is to encapsulate the tree/build logic into a dedicated type so the public utility methods stop managing node queues and traversal details directly.

I’m moving the construction and traversal details behind a dedicated `HuffmanTree` type now. That keeps `HuffmanCoding` focused on API validation and compatibility, and it makes the algorithm state less scattered across unrelated static helpers.

The structure is cleaner now: `HuffmanCoding` only validates inputs and exposes the entry points, while `HuffmanTree` owns queue construction, node composition, and traversal. I’m compiling and running the existing tests to verify that this stayed behavior-preserving.

Refactored [HuffmanCoding.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/033_huffman_coding/HuffmanCoding.java:8) so the public class is now just the API surface and validation layer. The actual algorithm state and behavior live inside a dedicated `HuffmanTree` type, which now owns node creation, priority-queue merging, and code generation. That removes a lot of static helper sprawl and groups the implementation around the thing it actually models.

I didn’t need to change [HuffmanCodingTest.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/033_huffman_coding/HuffmanCodingTest.java:4); the existing tests still cover the refactor.
